The Verses of the Elder Bhaddiya,
Son of Kāḷigodhā: “Those fine garments that were worn upon my elephant’s neck;”
He ate rice-gruel with pure meat as a sauce;
now he is fortunate and constant.
Delighting in what comes in his alms-bowl,
the son of Godhā, Bhaddiya, meditates without clinging.
Wearing robes of discarded rags, constant in effort,
delighting in what comes into his alms-bowl,
he meditates without clinging.
Bhaddiya was the son of Godhā.
An alms-collector, constant in practice... [and so forth].
One who wears only three robes and is constant...
[and so on] ...one who goes for alms from house to house in regular order and is constant.
... [he is] one who eats at a single sitting, one who is constant, ... [and so forth].
One who eats only from the alms-bowl with persistence...
one who refuses food after the meal time with persistence.
... [He is] a forest-dweller, one who is constant, ... [and so on].
A tree-dweller who is constant, ...
[and so on] ... an open-air dweller who is constant.
... [He is] a dweller in charnel grounds, one who is constant... [and so forth]...
One who is content with whatever seat is provided, constant in practice...
one who is a sitter, constant in practice.

Contented and constant...
secluded and constant.
... not associating, constant in practice, ... [and so on] ... [as above] ... not associating, constant in practice, ... [and so on] ...
Ardent in energy, constant...
having abandoned the bronze vessel weighing a hundred palas,
A golden bowl with a hundred stripes;
I took this clay bowl—
this was the second consecration.
Within high circular walls,
with strong watchtowers and gatehouses,
it was guarded by those bearing swords in hand.
Formerly I lived in fear;
now I am blessed, without terror,
having abandoned all fear and dread.
Bhaddiva, the son of Godhā, meditates having entered the forest,
firmly established in the aggregate of virtuous conduct.
Cultivating mindfulness and wisdom,
I gradually attained the destruction of all fetters.
… the elder Bhaddiya, son of Kāḷigodhā …
